title: How Much Do Real Estate Wholesalers Make Per Deal? (Real Numbers Inside)

sections.content: If you are thinking about getting into wholesaling, one of the first questions you probably have is simple: how much do real estate wholesalers make per deal? The short answer is anywhere from $5,000 to $20,000 on a typical deal — but experienced wholesalers regularly close deals worth $30,000 or more. The range is wide because several factors affect your final check. If you are brand new to the business, check out our [Wholesale Real Estate for Beginners: Complete Guide](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesale-real-estate-beginners-guide) to understand the full picture before diving into the numbers.
What Is a Wholesale Assignment Fee?

When you wholesale a property, you do not actually buy and sell the house. Instead, you sign a purchase contract with a motivated seller, then sell your rights to that contract to a cash buyer for a fee. That fee is called an assignment fee, and it is how wholesalers get paid. To understand exactly how this works, read our detailed breakdown in [Assignment of Contract Explained: How Wholesalers Get Paid](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/assignment-of-contract-explained). The assignment fee is the difference between what you agreed to pay the seller and what your cash buyer is willing to pay for the deal.
A Simple Example

Say you find a distressed property. The seller is motivated and agrees to accept $120,000. You run your numbers and know a cash buyer will pay $135,000 for that deal. You assign the contract for $135,000, the buyer pays the difference, and you walk away with a $15,000 assignment fee. No renovations, no mortgage, no holding costs. That is the core of wholesaling.
Average Wholesale Deal Profits: What the Numbers Actually Look Like

Industry data and self-reported income from wholesalers across the country suggest a fairly consistent range depending on market and experience level. Here is a realistic breakdown of what wholesalers earn per deal at different stages of their career.

items: Beginner wholesalers (0–1 year): $3,000–$8,000 per deal. Early deals often have thinner margins while you are still learning to negotiate and find deep discounts.
Intermediate wholesalers (1–3 years): $8,000–$20,000 per deal. You have a buyer list, a repeatable lead source, and stronger negotiation skills.
Experienced wholesalers (3+ years): $15,000–$40,000+ per deal. You are targeting bigger deals, commercial properties, or high-demand markets where spreads are wider.
Luxury or commercial wholesale deals: $50,000–$100,000+ per deal. These are less frequent but exist in markets like Atlanta, Houston, and Phoenix.

What Factors Affect How Much You Make Per Deal?

Your assignment fee is not random. It is the result of a formula: ARV minus repairs minus the buyer's profit minus your fee equals the seller's purchase price. Every variable in that equation shapes what you can earn. Here are the biggest factors that determine your per-deal profit.

items: Property ARV (After Repair Value): Higher-value homes create more room for larger fees. A $400,000 ARV property has more spread than a $100,000 ARV home.
Repair costs: Heavily distressed properties eat into the spread. Light cosmetic rehabs often produce the best wholesale margins.
How motivated the seller is: The deeper the discount you negotiate, the more room you have to build in your fee.
Your cash buyer's profit expectations: Experienced flippers typically want 20–30% ROI. If they need more room, your fee shrinks.

Local market demand: Hot markets like [Atlanta, GA](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/atlanta-ga), [Houston, TX](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/houston-tx), and [Phoenix, AZ](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/phoenix-az) have active buyer pools that compete for good deals, which can support higher fees.
Your buyer list strength: A deep bench of cash buyers means faster closings and sometimes bidding that raises your assignment fee above your initial ask.

sections.content: How Many Deals Can a Wholesaler Close Per Month?

One deal per month is a reasonable goal for a part-time beginner. Full-time wholesalers with systems in place often close 3–5 deals per month. At $10,000 per deal and 3 deals a month, that is $30,000 in monthly gross income — or $360,000 per year. Of course, expenses like marketing, skip tracing, and contract costs come out of that total. Most active wholesalers report net margins between 60–80% of their gross fees after expenses, which still makes wholesaling one of the highest-return entry points in real estate investing.
"The money in wholesaling is not in the deal you find — it is in the system you build to find deals consistently." — Common wisdom among experienced real estate wholesalers
How to Maximize Your Assignment Fee on Every Deal
Knowing the average is useful, but knowing how to push your fees higher is where real money is made. Here are the most effective strategies wholesalers use to earn more per deal.
1. Build a Strong Cash Buyer List

The bigger and more active your buyer list, the more leverage you have. When multiple buyers want the same deal, you can run a highest-and-best scenario that drives up your assignment fee naturally. Learn the best ways to grow your network in our guide on [How to Find Cash Buyers for Wholesale Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/how-to-find-cash-buyers-wholesale).
2. Negotiate Hard on the Front End

Your profit is locked in when you sign the seller contract, not when you assign it. Spend most of your energy getting the deepest discount possible on the seller side. Every extra $5,000 you negotiate off the purchase price goes directly into your assignment fee. Focus on truly motivated sellers: pre-foreclosures, probate, divorce, and tired landlords are your best sources.
3. Use the Right Contract

A solid, assignable contract protects your fee and prevents deals from falling apart at the closing table. Make sure your paperwork is airtight from the start. Check out our [How to Get a Wholesale Real Estate Contract (Free Template)](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/wholesale-real-estate-contract-template) to download a proven template you can use today.
4. Target the Right Markets

Not all markets are created equal for wholesalers. Cities with high investor activity, growing populations, and a strong rental market tend to support higher assignment fees. Sun Belt cities are particularly active right now. If you want to explore deeper dives into real estate investing strategy, our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide and [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide are great next reads.
Realistic Income Expectations for New Wholesalers

It is easy to see the big numbers online and expect to close a $30,000 deal in your first month. Most wholesalers take 60–90 days to close their first deal. Your first deal might net you $4,000–$7,000. That is not a failure — that is tuition. Each deal teaches you how to negotiate better, how to evaluate properties faster, and how to build relationships with buyers who will come back again and again. Consistent wholesalers with 2–3 years of experience can realistically earn $150,000–$300,000 per year, depending on their market and deal volume.

Pro Tip: Do not wait until you feel "ready" to make offers. Most wholesalers learn more from their first two or three deals than from months of studying. Get a deal under contract, work through the process, and let real experience teach you.
